issues.legal_issue: A firm claiming to be the tenant, together with its partners, may be joined as proper parties to an eviction proceeding when their presence would facilitate complete determination of the dispute.
material_facts: In an eviction proceeding, the applicant sought to be joined on the basis that the disputed premises had been let to a partnership firm and that the firm and its partners were tenants.
The landlords disputed that the firm was the tenant and relied on an earlier finding that an individual had been the tenant.
The competing contentions made the identity of the tenant relevant to determining the eviction dispute.
issues.conclusion: The firm and all its partners were proper parties and were impleaded as additional respondents. They were not necessary parties from the eviction petitioners’ point of view, but their presence would facilitate complete determination of the matter. The underlying tenancy questions were left open for the Rent Controller to decide.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order I Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court may add a proper party where that party’s presence would facilitate complete determination of the matter in dispute. A party need not be necessary from the plaintiff’s perspective to qualify as a proper party. The Court invoked this power suo motu. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.eviction_proceeding: The matter is an eviction proceeding.
predicates.disputed_identity_of_tenant: The parties dispute who held the tenancy.
predicates.proposed_parties_claim_tenancy_through_a: The proposed parties claim that a firm was the tenant and that they were its partners.
predicates.their_presence_would_facilitate_complete: The proposed parties’ participation would assist the court in completely determining the dispute.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding involves a dispute over the tenant’s identity, and a firm and its partners claim the tenancy and would assist complete determination, they are proper parties for joinder.
